subject: penguin
pitch: An emperor penguin chick's proud parent. Glossy blue-black back and head, a crisp white belly blending into a warm golden-yellow patch at the neck and ear, a long slender beak with an orange-pink stripe, stubby flippers held slightly out, and big black feet. A fluffy grey chick peeks out from between its feet.
reasoning:
I'm planning a compact penguin model: an adult emperor penguin around 1.15m tall with a small chick peeking out in front, built with a skeleton of root, pelvis, chest, neck, and head joints connected by sweep-based body parts.

Continuing joint placement for flippers, legs, and tail, then deciding to build the body with a loft using a single uniform-weight spine bone instead of a more complex rig for simplicity. For coloring, I'm setting up a paint function that shades the back dark, the belly white, and adds a golden gradient patch near the neck based on surface normal and height, blending smoothly rather than with hard edges.

Defining loft stations...

I'll shape the head as a scaled sphere with a dark paint, then add a golden ear patch and neck gradient using position-based smoothstep masks rather than decals. I'm setting up a shared plumage paint function that takes position and normal to blend dark and lighter tones across body and head.

Still working out the gold/dark masking...

Still refining gold/ear coloring...

Now I'm shaping the beak as a long, slightly down-curved tube with dark coloring and pink stripe sectors on both sides, attached near the head bone, and starting to define the lower jaw sweep similarly.

Lower beak gets a thinner orange-pink capsule tapering down. For eyes, I need contrast against the dark head, so I'm layering a small brown ring sphere behind a black pupil with a tiny white glint. Then I'm starting the flipper chains with shoulder, elbow, and tip joints on each side.

Working out the chain's local frame via the direction's cross product to get the normal axis, then reasoning about which way the flipper's broad flat face should orient—it hangs outward/inward so the wide dimension should align with that axis rather than depth.

Confirming the normal direction works out the same for both flippers, so I can pass up a fixed up-vector. Now I'm working out the flipper coloring: dark on the outer surface with a lighter white patch toward the inner edge, using the normal's x-sign relative to which side the flipper is on, then moving on to the leg geometry.

Now I'm sketching the legs and feet: short hidden legs with hip and ankle joints, dark gray coloring, and flattened ellipsoid feet with three fanned toe ellipsoids positioned to just touch the floor. I'm also starting the tail, defining a stiff wedge-shaped joint chain running from the base out to a tapered tip.

Now I'm positioning the body so it caps around y=0.2 with legs hidden beneath, and placing the baby chick peeking out between the parent's feet near the front of the belly. I'm working out the spacing so the feet sit wide enough apart (around ±0.09 to ±0.12 on x) for the fluffy gray chick body to nestle visibly between them without clipping.

The chick itself gets a small round body with a grey-toned head bearing the classic white face mask and black cap, plus a tiny dark cone beak and simple eyes, built from a few overlapping soft spheres to suggest downy fluff rather than sharp geometry. I'm setting up its joint hierarchy with a body and head node, deciding to skip a separate jaw joint since the chick doesn't need a working beak.

I'm positioning the chick so it nestles against the adult's belly, letting the body overlap slightly so it looks tucked in, and placing the head in front where it peeks out naturally. Overall creature height lands around 1.15 units with the body width a touch wider than a typical emperor penguin for a friendlier silhouette, and now I'm laying out the main joint chain—pelvis, spine, neck, head, and jaw—using chained joints to build the skeleton.

Adding leg chains for each side...

Legs end with a round cap, and I'm setting feet color to near-black. I'm thinking through how the flipper sweep radius should vary along its length using a bone chain.

Now I'm setting up eye sizes and preparing to use paint helper functions like mix and smoothstep from the SDK for coloring.

Writing plumage shading logic...

Still tuning gold/ear blending logic...

Now I'm setting up the chick's coloring, with grey body tones, a lighter front, and a dark cap mask on the head.

Adding chick eyes, a tiny black beak cone, and a fluffy ellipsoid body, plus thinking through spiky tufts arranged in a ring around the head.

Now I'm planning small capsule wings and bone joints for the chick, attaching a chick body joint to root and a chick head joint parented to it, then setting up loft stations with position, width, and height for the body shape.

I'm positioning the head sphere and neck transition relative to the body's top loft station, aligning radii so the neck smoothly tapers into the head before working out the beak's starting point.

Now I'm shaping the beak as two tapered lofts — a longer slender upper path and a shorter jaw path beneath it, both narrowing toward the tip, then setting up colored sectors to shade the upper beak surface.

Next I'm placing the eyes on the head's ellipsoid surface, computing offsets so the eye sphere, pupil, and glint sit correctly at a slight inward angle on each side.

I'll mirror this across left and right sides using a loop over the two sign values, then move on to writing the full shape out.
